entry.title: Package managers have an integrity problem
entry.summary:
I tested 25 of the most popular package managers to check whether they detect a compromised package repository injecting malicious code into legitimate packages. This code integrity problem could be solved using cryptographic hashes or signatures, but many package managers are still vulnerable to this threat. Of the 25 package managers reviewed 1 , fewer than half used lockfiles that checked for tampering by default, and only two verified the integrity of every package they downloaded.

Source: Trail of Bits Security Research · Tags: #infosec #cryptography #rust #databases

entry.title: Rethinking Zero-Knowledge TLS: Proof of Protocol Execution and the Reclaim Protocol
entry.summary:
In a zkTLS protocol, a user proves to a third party a property of data obtained from an online service over TLS, revealing nothing beyond the statement proven. Each existing scheme, however, comes with its own security model, written for that scheme alone, so the schemes are not proven secure against a common definition. The root cause is a mismatch of levels: existing models are stated at the level of TLS and therefore reflect how each construction handles it.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #rust #distributed-systems

entry.title: QUASI: Post-Quantum Quorum Attestation of Pre-Validated Statements
entry.summary:
We present QUASI, a newly conceived class of hash-based, post-quantum-secure protocols that enable a group of parties to produce a publicly verifiable attestation about a pre-validated statement. QUASI produces attestations that reduce the size and verification cost to a fraction of a full hash-based signatures collection, without relying on SNARKs or a trusted setup. QUASI rests on a surprising discovery: each party need not sign the entire statement.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #rust #consensus
